examples.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, hěn gāoxìng rènshi nǐ.

words.tip: Two third tones in a row: the first one rises, so it sounds like ní hǎo. Between friends people often skip it entirely.
Literally 'again see'. 明天见 (see you tomorrow) reuses 见, a nice pattern to show.
The second 谢 is toneless. Teach the reply too: 不客气 (bú kèqi, you're welcome).
Goes at the start of a request: 请坐, 请进 (please come in). Also 'to treat': 我请你 = my treat.
Roughly 'can't face you', a real apology. For a light 'excuse me' (getting attention, squeezing past), use 不好意思 (bù hǎoyìsi).
Same form for I and me. Add 的 for 'my' (我的). Pronouns never change form in Chinese, a relief after German.
The left side 亻 is the 'person' radical. Polite 'you' is 您 (nín), a bit like German Sie.
Sounds exactly like 她 (she). Only the written radical differs: 亻 person.
Same sound as 他 (he). The 女 radical means 'woman'. In speech you can't tell them apart either.
们 makes any pronoun plural: 我们, 你们, 他们. 咱们 (zánmen) means 'we, including you', common in the north.
Links nouns (我是德国人) but not adjectives: say 我很累, never 我是累. It never changes form.
Always negated with 没, never 不: 没有. Also means 'there is': 这里有咖啡 (there's coffee here).
Do and make, like German machen. 做饭 = to cook. Watch out for 作, which has the same sound.
No 'to' needed: 去 + place (去中国, 去超市). 吧 at the end turns it into 'let's'.
Movement towards the speaker, the opposite of 去.
Question words sit where the answer would go: 这是什么? = 'this is what?'. No word-order change, unlike German and English.
Two pronunciations: shéi (common in speech) and shuí. Both are correct.
Only the tone separates 哪里 (where) from 那里 (nàlǐ, there). Northern speakers say 哪儿 (nǎr). Also a modest reply to a compliment: 哪里哪里!
Literally 'what time'. It goes before the verb: 你什么时候来?

examples.english: How do you read this character?

words.tip: Useful extras: 怎么了? = what's wrong? 怎么样? = how is it? / how about it?
Chinese has no all-purpose 'yes'. You repeat the verb (你去吗? 去!) or say 对 (that's right).
Becomes bú before a 4th tone: 不是 (bú shì), 不要 (bú yào). Used for habits, preferences and the future.
Negates 有 and completed actions: 我没去 (I didn't go). The 不 vs 没 contrast is worth a few examples.
Always before the verb, never at the end of the sentence like English 'too'.
Often just links a subject and an adjective with little 'very' meaning: 我很好 = I'm good. Stress it to mean 'really'.
Show the family: 今天 today, 明天 tomorrow, 昨天 (zuótiān) yesterday.
明 = sun 日 + moon 月, 'bright'. The same pattern gives 明年 = next year.
Time words go near the start, before the verb: 我现在很忙.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài Běijīng zhù le sān tiān.
examples.english: We stayed in Beijing for three days.

words.tip: Also 'sky' and 'heaven'. Counts on its own with no measure word: 三天 = three days.
Counts on its own like 天: 两年. Chinese New Year (春节, Chūnjié) is a great thing to talk about together.
你吃饭了吗? is a classic friendly greeting, not an invitation. The 口 (mouth) radical shows up in lots of mouth words.

examples.english: What would you like to drink?

words.tip: Another 口 radical. Common pairs: 喝水, 喝茶, 喝酒 (drink alcohol).

examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì bēi shuǐ.
examples.english: Please give me a glass of water.

words.tip: Many Chinese people drink 热水 (hot water) by default, a good talking point next to German Kohlensäure.
Means both rice and 'a meal': 早饭 breakfast, 午饭 lunch, 晚饭 dinner. 米饭 is specifically rice.
German Tee and English 'tea' come from a southern Chinese pronunciation (tê), 'chai' from chá. Black tea is 红茶, 'red tea'.
Means both home and family. The character is a roof 宀 over a pig 豕, a memorable picture.
间 is also the measure word for rooms. 卧室 (wòshì) = bedroom.
The character looks like a doorway. 开门 / 关门 = open / close the door, and also a shop opening or closing. 个 is fine in casual speech.
住在 + place: 我住在… Like German wohnen, it's about where you live, not being alive (活).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào shàng chuáng shuìjiào le.

words.tip: 张 is the measure word for flat things: beds, tables, paper. 起床 = get up.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ māma zuò de fàn hěn hǎochī.

words.tip: The second syllable is toneless. 母亲 (mǔqīn) is the formal word. Note the 女 radical again.
Same pattern as 妈妈. 父亲 (fùqīn) is formal.
Use 两 (not 二) for 'two' before a measure word: 两个孩子.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de hǎo péngyou.

words.tip: 男朋友 = boyfriend, 女朋友 = girlfriend, the same idea as German Freund / Freundin.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jiārén dōu zài Déguó.
examples.english: My family are all in Germany.

words.tip: 家 (from the home session) + 人 person. A good moment to show how words are built from characters already known.

examples.english: I want a cup of coffee.

words.tip: Direct 'want', also 'going to': 我要走了 = I'm off now. 不要 = don't (want).

examples.english: I'd like to go to China.

words.tip: Softer than 要, like German möchte. Also 'think' and 'miss': 我想你 = I miss you.
喜欢 + verb = like doing, the job German gern does. Works for people too: 我喜欢你.
Literally 'high mood'. 很高兴认识你 = nice to meet you, a callback to session 1.
累死了 = exhausted (lit. tired to death), the same exaggeration as German todmüde.
女 woman + 子 child = good, a classic picture. 好 + verb means 'nice to': 好吃 (tasty), 好看 (good-looking).
A person with arms stretched wide. Also age: 你多大? = how old are you (to peers and adults).
Also a friendly nickname prefix: 小王 = 'little Wang'. 太…了 = too…

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de xīn shǒujī.

words.tip: Already seen in 新年快乐. Goes straight before short nouns without 的: 新书, 新车.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de lǎo péngyou.
examples.english: He's an old friend of mine.

words.tip: For people and relationships (老朋友, 老师). Old things use 旧 (jiù): 旧手机. As a prefix it's affectionate: 老王.
The tone shifts: yí before a 4th tone (一个 yí ge), yì before the others (一天 yì tiān), yī when counting or alone.
For counting and in numbers (二十 = 20, 二月 = February). Before a measure word use 两 instead: 两个人.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu sān kǒu rén.
examples.english: There are three people in my family.

words.tip: One, two, three are just one, two, three strokes. 口 (mouth) is the measure word for family members.
Sounds like 死 (sǐ, death), so 4 is unlucky and some buildings skip the 4th floor. Tongue twister: 四是四，十是十.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen wǔ ge rén qù chīfàn.
examples.english: The five of us are going to eat.

words.tip: Show the one-handed Chinese counting gestures for 1–10. They're different from German finger counting.
Before a measure word many people say zhèi: 这个 zhège / zhèige. Both are fine.
那 (nà, that) and 哪 (nǎ, which) differ by tone, and 哪 has the 口 radical that marks many question words.
Northern speakers say 这儿 (zhèr). Same pattern as 哪里 from session 4.
Northern: 那儿 (nàr). Only the tone separates it from 哪里 (nǎlǐ, where), so drill the pair.

examples.english: The book is on the table.

words.tip: Says where something is: 我在这里. Before a verb it means 'in the middle of': 我在吃饭 = I'm eating.

examples.english: You and I will go together.

words.tip: Only joins nouns (我和你), never two sentences, unlike German und. Many speakers say 跟 (gēn) instead.

examples.english: Do you drink tea or coffee?

words.tip: 'Or' in questions. In statements use 或者 (huòzhě): 茶或者咖啡都可以 = tea or coffee are both fine.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn lèi, dànshì hěn gāoxìng.

words.tip: Often shortened to 但. 可是 (kěshì) is a softer spoken alternative.

examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, wǒmen zài jiā.
examples.english: Because it's raining, we're staying home.

words.tip: The 'because' part normally comes first, whereas German usually puts the weil part second. Often paired with 所以.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn lèi, suǒyǐ zǎo diǎn shuì.
examples.english: I'm tired, so I'll go to bed early.

words.tip: Chinese happily says 因为… 所以… in one sentence ('because…, so…'), which sounds doubled up in English and German.

examples.english: How do you say it in Chinese?

words.tip: 用中文怎么说? is the most useful sentence for these sessions. 讠 is the 'speech' radical.

words.gloss: to look, to watch, to read
words.tip: A hand 手 over an eye 目, shading your eyes to look. Also read (看书) and visit (看朋友).
听说… = I heard that… 听懂 = to understand by listening.
Knowing facts, like German wissen. In speech 道 is often toneless: zhīdao.
Knowing people, like German kennen. Also recognising characters: 你认识这个字吗?

examples.english: I can speak a little Chinese.

words.tip: For learned skills (languages, swimming), and 'will probably': 明天会下雨 = it'll probably rain tomorrow.
Ability or circumstances allowing. 会 (know how), 能 (able) and 可以 (allowed) make a great trio to explain.
Permission, like German dürfen. 可以! on its own = sure, OK. Two 3rd tones: sounds like kéyǐ.

examples.english: You should go to bed earlier.

words.tip: Advice or expectation, like German sollen. Also 'probably': 他应该到了 = he should be there by now.
Strong necessity. 'Don't have to' is 不用 (bú yòng), not 不必须, the same trap as German muss nicht.

examples.pinyin: Shànghǎi shì yí ge dà chéngshì.

words.tip: A walled market: 城 (wall) + 市 (market). Talk about which cities each of you has lived in.
条 is the measure word for long thin things: roads, rivers, fish. 一路平安 = have a safe trip.

examples.pinyin: Tā de chē shì xīn de.

words.tip: Any vehicle: 汽车 (car), 火车 (train, 'fire vehicle'), 自行车 (bicycle). Driving yourself is 开车.
Sitting, and riding as a passenger: 坐车, 坐飞机. Two people 人人 on the ground 土. Same sound as 做 (do).
Literally 'vehicle stand'. 火车站 = train station, 地铁站 = metro station.
Both a noun and a verb. The place comes before the verb: 在 + place + 工作.
Learning plus practising. 学 alone works too: 学中文.
大学 (dàxué) = university, 'big learning'. 个 works as the measure word in speech.
看书 = to read. 书店 = bookshop.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de Zhōngwén lǎoshī.

words.tip: Also how you address a teacher: 王老师. Fitting, since you're each other's 老师 now.

examples.pinyin: Xià ge xīngqī wǒmen qù Běijīng.
examples.english: Next week we're going to Beijing.

words.tip: Days are numbered: 星期一 is Monday through 星期六 Saturday. Sunday is 星期天 or 星期日.
早! on its own is a casual 'morning!'. 早饭 = breakfast.
Covers evening and night. 晚安 (wǎn'ān) = good night, said at bedtime like Gute Nacht.
几点? = what time is it? 三点半 = 3:30, so no German-style 'half to four'. 一点儿 = a little.
Time as an amount, like German Zeit. Clock time uses 点. 没有时间 = no time.
买 (mǎi, buy) and 卖 (mài, sell) differ only by tone and the 十 on top. Drill them as a pair.
Falling tone, the partner of 买. 买卖 (mǎimai, 'buy-sell') = business.
The 钅 radical means metal, because early money was metal. Prices use 块 (kuài) in speech, 元 (yuán) in writing.
Literally 'many-few'. 多少钱? is the shopping question. For small numbers people use 几 (jǐ) instead.
太贵了! is essential at markets. Also 'honourable': 您贵姓? = may I ask your surname?
A lucky number: 六 sounds like 流 (flowing smoothly), so 666 means 'awesome' online.

examples.pinyin: Yí ge xīngqī yǒu qī tiān.

words.tip: Note the q, which sounds like 'ch' in 'cheese'. A good one for practising pinyin spelling.
The luckiest number: 八 sounds like 发 (fā, to prosper). The Beijing Olympics opened at 8:08 pm on 8/8/2008.
Sounds like 久 (jiǔ, long-lasting), so it's popular around weddings.
Bigger numbers are perfectly regular: 十一 = 11, 二十 = 20, 九十九 = 99. Compare German neunundneunzig, which says the ones first.

examples.english: There are lots of people here.

words.tip: A person walking on two legs. Nationalities add 人: 德国人 (German), 中国人 (Chinese).
男 is a field 田 over strength 力: the one working the field. 男朋友 = boyfriend.
Note the ü in nǚ. The 女 radical has turned up in 她, 妈妈 and 好.

examples.english: The girl is reading a book.

words.tip: Also 女孩子. Boy = 男孩. Fun contrast: German das Mädchen is grammatically neuter.
Surnames come first: 王小明 = Wang Xiaoming. Talk about what each of your names means.
Turns anything into 'X's': 我的 (my), 妈妈的 (mum's). Often dropped for close family and friends: 我妈妈.
Like German ihr (you all). Same 们 as 我们 from session 2.
她们 for an all-female group; mixed groups use 他们. All sound the same.
Adds 'myself / yourself': 你自己去吧 = go by yourself. 自己的 = one's own.
Literally 'big family'. Matches German alle. 大家好 opens almost every speech.
A verb-plus-object pair that can be split: 睡了一个好觉 = had a good sleep. 觉 is read jué in 觉得 (session 26).
Reading aloud, or studying (读大学 = go to university). Reading for fun is often just 看书.

examples.english: How do you write this character?

words.tip: 这个字怎么写? will be your most-asked question. Practise stroke order together.

examples.english: The kids are playing in the park.

words.tip: Also 'hang out': 周末去哪儿玩? Sports and instruments use other verbs (打篮球, 弹钢琴), unlike German spielen.
等一下 = wait a moment. At the end of a list it means 'etc.'

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ yì běn shū.

words.tip: Also 'for / to': 给你打电话 = call you. 给你! = here you go.
There's a hand 手 at the bottom. 拿走 = take away, 拿来 = bring over.

examples.english: Don't forget to bring your keys.

words.tip: Taking something or someone with you. 带孩子 = to look after the kids.
帮忙 (bāngmáng) is the 'help out' form: 谢谢你帮忙. 帮我 + verb = do something for me.
Stronger than 要. 不需要 = no need.
Opinions and feelings, like German glauben or finden. 我觉得很好 = I think it's good.

examples.text: 我可以问你一个问题吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ wèn nǐ yí ge wèntí ma?
examples.english: Can I ask you a question?

words.tip: A mouth 口 inside a door 门: asking at the door. 问题 = question; 没问题 = no problem.
告诉 + person + thing. 我告诉你 = let me tell you.
听懂 = understand by listening, 看懂 = understand by reading. 我不懂 = I don't get it.
A learner's best friend: …是什么意思? Also 有意思 = interesting, 不好意思 = excuse me.
Literally 'sky air'. 天气预报 = weather forecast.
阳 is the 'yang' of yin and yang. The older word 日 lives on in 日本 (Japan, 'sun's origin').
Rain 'falls down': 下雨, and snow is 下雪. No 'it' needed, unlike German es regnet.
The four dots at the bottom (灬) mean fire. 热水 (hot water) came up in session 7.
The two strokes on the left (冫) mean ice. 我很冷 = I'm cold, simpler than German Mir ist kalt.
The colour of luck: red envelopes (红包) at New Year. Add 色 for the colour as a noun: 红色.
The grass radical 艹 on top: blue dye originally came from a plant.
Another ü: lǜ. 绿茶 (green tea) from session 7.
Fire 灬 at the bottom: soot. 天黑了 = it's got dark.
Also 'for nothing': 白跑一趟 = a wasted trip. 明白 (clear and bright) = to understand.
Goes before the verb like other adverbs. 一直 (yìzhí) means 'all along, continuously'.
Doubled for emphasis. 经常 (jīngcháng) means the same.
For past experiences use 从来没…过: 我从来没去过德国 = I've never been to Germany.
Usually paired with 了 at the end: 已经…了.
Still, also, and 还没 = not yet: 我还没吃. The same character as in 还是 (session 14).
…疼 = …hurts: 头疼, 肚子疼 (stomach ache). 头 is also the measure word for cattle.
手机 = mobile phone ('hand machine'), just like German Handy.
A pair of eyes: 一双眼睛. The 目 radical (an eye) also appears in 看.
The 疒 radical means illness (also in 疼). 多喝热水 (drink lots of hot water) is the classic advice!

examples.english: I need to see a doctor.

words.tip: 看医生 = to see a doctor. 医院 = hospital.
